text.p: The following are top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Mid-air collision kills 349 people and expert says main radar at New Delhi airport cannot trace altitude of outgoing jets.
- All licensed dogs will have electronic identification soon.
- Civil servants may not receive special bonuses this year in view of economic slowdown.
- Some banks 'poaching' housing loans from rival lending institutions as slowing demand intensifies competition in sluggish residential property market.
- Bids below benchmark levels in latest land tender, at 10-18 percent below expectations.
- Malaysia Securities Commission chairman Mohd Munir Abdul Majod announces at seminar that Malaysia will liberalise dealing and harmonise futures markets.
- Sound card maker Aztech Systems may face damages and legal costs of between Singapore $20 million and $40 million in copyright battle against Creative Technology.
- Fashion group FJ Benjamin's initial public offering is 29.9 times subscribed.
- U.S. Rederal Reserve decides to hold interest rates steady at policy-making meeting.
- Hong Leong Group says it is interested in the Hong Kong $11 billion third-phase of Tung Chung airport/railway-station development.
- Trading in Malayan Credit Limited announces its surge to 4.2 million shares.
- Singapore Stock Exchange announces that many of Singapore's listed comapnies will have to replace some members of audit committees as a result of new definitions of independent directors.

- Marine-based conglomerate Sembawang Corporation announces subsidiary Sembawang Industrial Pte Ltd has sold entire holdings of 18.78 million First Capital Corporation warrants to Hong Kong listed Guoco Investment for Singapore $35.67 million or $1.90 each.
